query: Help me understand what's in these airline reviews — I'm not sure which aspect is most worth analyzing.

per_column.name: cabin_crew_attitude
per_column.rationale: Rich qualitative categorization of crew behaviour (friendly/rude/cold_robotic/neutral/mixed) that adds a real interpretive axis beyond the numeric Staff Service rating, and is highly relevant to an exploratory 'which aspect matters' query. Groundedness is only moderate: it correctly reads samples 1,3,4,5 where crew is described, and the column does emit NULLs, but sample 2 (a review purely about seat/entertainment, silent on crew) was assigned 'rude_dismissive' — a sentiment-halo inference the text does not support, where 'unknown' would have been correct.

per_column.name: food_quality_signal
per_column.rationale: Useful qualitative food axis with distinctive categories (special_meal_failure, meal_not_served) that go beyond the existing numeric Food & Beverages column, though it partly overlaps it. Groundedness is weak: samples 1,3,4 correctly extract food praise, but sample 2 ('poor_quality') and sample 5 ('adequate') invent food judgments for reviews that never mention food, despite the column clearly being capable of NULL — a negative/positive halo rather than a grounded reading.

per_column.name: service_decline_perception
per_column.rationale: Near-constant boolean (94% false) and conceptually near-duplicate of airline_decline_narrative, so it offers little grouping/modelling leverage for this query. The False values shown are consistent with the sample texts (none assert decline), so from the visible evidence it is not fabricating, but the analytical payoff is low.

per_column.name: amenity_and_product_gap
per_column.rationale: The amenity/product angle is a plausibly new dimension, but the label is vague and the values appear driven by overall sentiment rather than explicit amenity mentions. The column emits very few NULLs (350) yet the sample reviews rarely discuss amenity kits/products: sample 2 asserts 'amenities_absent' and samples 3/5 assert 'full_amenities_provided' with no direct textual support, indicating confident specifics where the text is largely silent.

per_column.name: ground_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Captures a genuinely distinct aspect (check-in/gate/ground handling) not represented in the original numeric ratings, giving the analyst a fresh axis. Groundedness is strong: all five samples, none of which mention ground service, are correctly left 'Unknown'/NULL — appropriate abstention rather than fabrication.

per_column.name: disruption_handling_quality
per_column.rationale: A new and analytically valuable dimension (how delays/cancellations were handled) with a clear not_applicable option. In all samples, which describe undisrupted flights, it correctly returns not_applicable, showing sound conditional behaviour and no unsupported assertions in the evidence.

per_column.name: cs_resolution_quality
per_column.rationale: Adds a customer-service resolution axis absent from the originals; somewhat narrow (mostly not_contacted) but still a legitimate grouping variable. Groundedness is good: the samples never mention contacting the airline and are correctly marked not_contacted.

per_column.name: airline_decline_narrative
per_column.rationale: Near-constant (94% false) and effectively a restatement of service_decline_perception, so it provides little independent analytical leverage. The False labels are consistent with the sample texts, so no fabrication is visible, but the column is largely redundant.

per_column.name: premium_cabin_value_judgment
per_column.rationale: Overlaps heavily with the existing Value For Money and Class columns, offering only a modest premium-specific angle. More seriously, it is poorly grounded: it applies premium-cabin verdicts to economy passengers — sample 4 explicitly states 'flying in economy class' yet is scored 'exceeds_expectations', and sample 1 (short-haul economy) likewise; a 'not_applicable' would be correct, so several values contradict or ignore stated class information.

judge.rationale: For an open-ended 'which aspect is worth analyzing' query, the set does provide several genuinely useful new axes: cabin_crew_attitude, ground_service_quality, disruption_handling_quality and cs_resolution_quality surface aspects not captured by the original numeric ratings and give real grouping/comparison leverage. Usefulness is pulled down by two near-constant, mutually redundant booleans (service_decline_perception and airline_decline_narrative) and by premium_cabin_value_judgment, which largely restates existing Value/Class fields. On groundedness the picture is mixed: the conditionally-scoped columns (ground/disruption/cs) show excellent abstention discipline, correctly returning Unknown/not_applicable/not_contacted for silent rows, but the sentiment-driven columns exhibit a clear halo problem — cabin_crew_attitude, food_quality_signal, amenity_and_product_gap and premium_cabin_value_judgment assign confident positive/negative values on rows where the source text is silent (or, for premium value, contradicts a stated economy cabin). This fabrication pattern in several columns is the main groundedness weakness.
